incidents.victim: Southeast Asian critical infrastructure (electricity, water, government, military)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-language group deployed a stealthy C# backdoor disguised as a Visual Studio telemetry binary plus renamed SoftEther VPN tooling, moving laterally across agencies within the same country.
incidents.impact: Researchers documented 10+ intrusions compromising regional electricity and water providers, government and military organizations, and two state-owned entities; assessed as espionage or pre-positioning for future access. Activity continues at reduced volume.

incidents.vector: An out-of-bounds memory read (CVE-2026-8451) is triggered by malformed SAML authentication requests to NetScaler appliances configured as SAML identity providers; disclosed alongside five other NetScaler flaws.
incidents.impact: Citrix disclosed a high-severity memory-disclosure flaw echoing the earlier CitrixBleed, plus vulnerabilities enabling denial of service and unauthenticated file reads. No confirmed exploitation of the new flaw at disclosure, though a related March CVE was actively exploited.

incidents.victim: Schneider Electric EasyLogic T150 and Saitel DP RTU users
incidents.vector: Insufficiently protected credentials (CVE-2026-9650) and incorrect permission assignment (CVE-2026-9651) let an attacker recover credentials and password hashes stored in firmware or system files.
incidents.impact: CISA advised that the flaws in Schneider Electric RTU/controller firmware could allow unauthorized device access and compromise. Vendor fixes are available and no public exploitation has been reported.

incidents.victim: Government officials, military personnel, journalists, and Ukraine-based officials
incidents.attacker: Russia — FSB and military intelligence services
incidents.vector: Social engineering impersonating messaging-app support tricks high-value targets into sharing verification codes, PINs, and backup recovery keys; altered Signal group-invite pages link attacker-controlled devices to victim accounts.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA warned of an ongoing campaign hijacking individual Signal and WhatsApp accounts to read historical private and group messages; the US posted a $10 million Rewards for Justice bounty. Recovery keys remain valid even after accounts are re-created.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical, and military research organizations
incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor ran a sophisticated targeted campaign against cross-sector research organizations that went undetected for more than a year.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group identified a prolonged intrusion campaign against North American academic, medical, and military research entities for cross-sector intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: A financially motivated extortion group exploited Oracle PeopleSoft application infrastructure to compromise victims.
incidents.impact: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence identified an active compromise-and-extortion campaign targeting Oracle PeopleSoft deployments in the education sector.

incidents.vector: A threat actor exploited a zero-day in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to escalate privileges from a compromised administrative account to root-level access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant identified active zero-day exploitation allowing attackers to gain root-level control of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Browser users installing malicious extensions (2.6M+ downloads)
incidents.vector: 119 malicious Edge extensions (plus Chrome and Firefox variants) offered genuine functionality but deployed steganography-hidden payloads 3-5 days after install to steal credentials, backdoor browsers, and commit ad and search fraud.
incidents.impact: Microsoft removed 119 Edge extensions from its store; an estimated 2.6M+ users had downloaded the operator's extensions. The group has been active since at least 2021.

incidents.victim: Browser users targeted by a Perplexity-spoofing extension
incidents.vector: A malicious Chromium extension spoofed Perplexity AI branding via a typosquatted domain and Manifest V3 rules to intercept Omnibox search queries and keystroke-level suggestions through attacker-controlled infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence found the extension conducting search-traffic interception and keystroke-level data collection; it was reported to Google and taken down.

incidents.victim: John R. Bolton (former US National Security Advisor) / US national defense information
incidents.vector: Compromise of Bolton's personal email account, which he had used to store and transmit classified diary entries to unauthorized family members.
incidents.impact: Bolton pleaded guilty to willfully retaining national defense information; DOJ stated the hacked account held top-secret material an Iran-linked actor accessed, exposing US military plans, covert operations, and clandestine-source intelligence.

incidents.vector: USB drives infected with Chinese-linked malware were connected to classified military networks.
incidents.impact: The breach went undisclosed for nearly a year; the stolen data remains unclear, and Japanese officials began notifying NATO partners of a possible leak.

incidents.vector: Breach of KDDI's public email service, which is also used by five other Japanese ISPs.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole the data of more than 14 million users.

incidents.vector: The Amadey loader served as an initial entry point to deploy the StealC infostealer, sold as malware-as-a-service on underground forums.
incidents.impact: A Europol-led operation with seven law-enforcement agencies and six security firms seized 326 servers, 142 domains, and over $47M in illicit crypto tied to operations that had infected 140,000+ computers and stolen 27M+ credentials.

incidents.vector: Breach of a third-party vendor that loaded malicious code onto the Polymarket website.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole roughly $3 million before detection; Polymarket pledged to reimburse affected users.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting a subsidiary handling engineering and research.
incidents.impact: Operations at one of India's largest automakers were disrupted; the company disclosed the incident to market authorities.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting the operator's mobile app and web services.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's state postal service had its mobile app and some web services knocked offline while it worked to restore service.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL-VPN gateways (global)
incidents.vector: Mass scanning and brute-forcing escalated into exploitation of old unpatched CVEs and a credential-interception script across many protocols; harvested SSL-VPN hashes were cracked on a GPU cluster (tracked as FortiBleed).
incidents.impact: One of the largest confirmed FortiGate credential exposures on record — roughly 74,000 device credential sets across 194 countries were leaked publicly and sold to other groups; a Turkish NATO defense contractor allegedly had documents exfiltrated. UK and Australian agencies issued critical alerts urging credential rotation, patching, and MFA.

incidents.vector: Breach of a third-party vendor managing the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a series of attacks targeting Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole names, phone numbers, and email addresses of Belgian intelligence-service employees.

incidents.vector: Members of an English-speaking SIM-swapping and social-engineering crew ran unauthorized intrusions into TfL computer systems in an August 2024 attack.
incidents.impact: Two UK members pleaded guilty to conspiring against TfL systems and causing risk of serious damage to human welfare; the attack crippled TfL operations. Both are slated for sentencing on July 15, 2026.

incidents.vector: The same English-speaking cybercrime crew conspired to intrude into US healthcare provider networks in September 2024 using social engineering and credential theft.
incidents.impact: A defendant admitted conspiring to hack these US healthcare providers as part of a guilty plea; the broader group is tied to roughly 120 intrusions across 47 US entities and at least $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Data theft by an extortion group that listed Tata Electronics as a victim on its leak site.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach; the group claims to have stolen 200,000+ documents allegedly containing sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (Salesforce data) — ~20 firms incl. Recorded Future, Snyk, LastPass, Huntress, Tanium, BeyondTrust
incidents.vector: Compromise of a legacy credential on the business-intelligence platform Klue, then theft of OAuth tokens connecting Klue to customers' Salesforce accounts, enabling bulk data download.
incidents.impact: Roughly 20 companies had Salesforce data stolen via the Klue supply-chain breach; the extortion group is pressuring Klue and threatening to leak the data. The victim list continues to grow.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a widely integrated product-review widget injected JavaScript that ran a ClickFix lure prompting users to paste malicious commands into their terminal.
incidents.impact: A supply-chain compromise affecting 18,000+ stores served infostealer/RAT payloads via ClickFix; the widget was restored to a safe version on May 14.

incidents.victim: Brazil national emergency alert system (Defesa Civil Nacional)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the national alert system used to broadcast an extreme-level alert.
incidents.impact: A hacker sent a false extreme-level alert across five regions including São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Brasília; the government took the alert system offline.

incidents.victim: Consumers running unofficial Android TV boxes (Popa / Vo1d botnet)
incidents.vector: Millions of unofficial Android TV boxes were enrolled via a bundled SDK tied to the Vo1d botnet into a residential proxy network relaying traffic for ad fraud, account takeovers, and mass data scraping.
incidents.impact: Researchers linked the Popa proxy network to a commercial residential-proxy provider; scraping events in May 2026 spanned 1.4 million IPs. The named commercial operator disputes the botnet characterization.

incidents.victim: Four major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat, Export Development Bank of Iran)
incidents.vector: Attack targeting communications infrastructure shared by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were down over a weekend; the banking council said no customer data was accessed. Intelligence sources later attributed the attack to Israeli hackers.

incidents.victim: Chinese domestic internet users (Silver Fox / Winos trojan victims)
incidents.vector: Malspam campaigns and fake app-download sites lured victims into installing the Silver Fox trojan, which deployed infostealers and custom RATs.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces tied to what authorities called the country's largest cybercrime group, including the malware author.
